title: Exponential semidefinite complexity for perfect matching
exact_target: For every fixed shift $\rho \in (0,1)$, do the matrices indexed by odd vertex sets U and perfect matchings M, with entry $|M\cap \delta (U)|-1+\rho $, where $\delta (U)$ is the set of edges crossing U, of complete graphs on even n vertices require real positive-semidefinite factorization rank at least $2^{cn}$, for one $c>0$ independent of $\rho $ and all sufficiently large n depending on $\rho $? This also asks for the resulting exponential exact semidefinite-lift lower bound.
